slides.title: The clocks: frame, fixed step and tick
slides.source: Source: Chapter 1, “Similarities”; Chapter 4, “Two clocks”, tick groups; glossary, Engine vocabulary.
slides.notes: Tick counts are computed over one second at 144 frames a second: 144 per frame; 60 fixed steps (16.7 ms) for Godot; 50 (20 ms) for Unity. Hand check: 1000 / 60 = 16.67, 1000 / 50 = 20.
slides.picture: Strips of tick marks over one second at 144 frames a second: frame ticks, a 60 a second fixed step for Godot, a 50 a second fixed step for Unity, and Unreal's two tick groups.

slides.title: Layer and mask, matrix, object type
slides.source: Source: Chapter 4, “Layers work differently” and “Collision is a response table”; glossary, Engine vocabulary; Game movement and collision.
slides.notes: Grid computed from each engine’s rule: Godot 2 of 6 directed pairs, Unity 4 of 6, Unreal 2 of 6. The Player-to-Mob cell in Unreal is the silent failure the chapter describes.
slides.picture: A three by three grid of Player, Mob and Coin. A tick means the row object notices the column object. Godot's mask is one way, Unity's matrix works both ways, and in Unreal both sides must agree.

new_texts: Each object has a layer and a mask. A notices B if B's layer is in A's mask: one way.
Player mask = Mob + Coin. Mob and Coin mask nothing.
Godot lets one side watch another without being watched.

slides.title: Before you port an idea between engines
slides.source: Source: Chapters 0 to 15, “Doing the same thing” sections.
slides.picture: A checklist of six items drawn one at a time.

new_texts: Am I using this engine's word: node, GameObject or Actor?
Which clock: per frame, or fixed (60 a second in Godot, 50 in Unity)?
Which way is up, and are the units metres or centimetres?
Does contact work from one side, or do both sides have to agree?
Is the asset text I can diff, or binary I must open the editor for?
Was it run, or only read from docs? The chapters ran neither Unity nor Unreal.
Then say it exactly: not “make it work in Unity”, but “tick Is Trigger and add a Rigidbody2D”.
